method: Fixed before reading: prior reactions set size (median |move|, cross-checked against 20d realised vol); direction comes only from run-up versus what is plausibly priced, plus reaction-sign momentum. Zacks-style previews are legible and assumed priced. Default Neutral unless two independent signals align.
key_drivers: Three consecutive negative reactions (-5.6, -14.0, -25.5); persistent DAU/guidance deceleration regime
Consensus EPS 61c implies -33% y/y on +17.9% revenue: margin compression is the story, guidance is the swing
Stock -65% from 52w high already prices heavy disappointment, capping downside asymmetry
No run-up to fade (-3.5% 5d), so the setup is closer to two-sided than the sign pattern suggests
Median |move| 13.9%, 20d vol 60.6% - a very wide, low-confidence distribution
what_would_change_my_mind: Evidence that DAU growth or bookings had already re-accelerated, which would break the serial-disappointment regime that is the whole of my directional tilt.
reasoning: Base rate is 5 of 8 negative and the last three all negative, in a name whose problem (decelerating users, AI-driven cost) compounds quarter over quarter. Against that, a 65% de-rating means the bar is low and no run-up needs fading, so I keep the tilt small. Sizing is driven by realised vol (60%) and a 13.9% median historical move; recent prints ran 5.6 to 25.5, so I set 12.5% rather than the median. The Zacks preview (+9.02% ESP, Rank 2) is exactly the legible material I discounted in advance. Certainty Low: this is a wide distribution and my edge is a weak sign-momentum effect only.

20d vol 55% against a 3.7% historical median implies a fatter move than the base rate alone
what_would_change_my_mind: A large unfaded run-up into the print, or a fresh data-centre PPA already announced pre-print, either of which would tell me the good news was in the price.
reasoning: My two directional inputs point mildly opposite ways to nothing: the sign pattern is a coin flip and the 20d drawdown into the print is a mild positive, so the method's own rule returns Neutral. The Zacks piece confirms strong 2026 estimate growth and the closed 2.6 GW acquisition, but that is precisely the widely-known material I pre-committed to treating as priced. For size I override the 3.7% median: realised vol of 55% annualised is roughly 3.5% a day, and an IPP levered to data-centre power demand does not move a typical utility's earnings move, so 5.5%. Certainty Low, evidence thin - one usable article and no filings read.

key_drivers: +17.5% in the five sessions into the print - the largest run-up in the batch, and the signal I trust most
Both prior prints entered on strength dropped hard (-20.7% Feb, -14.7% Nov)
Bull case is entirely legible: Q1 surprise ~289%, guidance raised to $450-500m, $3.8bn backlog, $900m DOE HALEU order
20d vol 81% and a 16.1% median move - direction is a small tilt inside an enormous distribution
Lumpy SWU delivery timing makes the headline number a poor guide to the reaction; guidance drives it
what_would_change_my_mind: If the 17.5% run-up were sector beta rather than name-specific positioning, the raised-bar argument that carries my entire tilt would dissolve.
reasoning: Two of my pre-committed signals align down: a sharp run-up into the print raising the bar, and a name whose two most recent hot entries were punished. The available news confirms an exceptionally strong and widely-circulated fundamental story - HALEU monopoly, raised guidance, large backlog - which under my method counts against the long side rather than for it, because it is the definition of already priced. Size dominates direction here: 81% realised vol and a 16.1% median historical move mean a 14% expected magnitude with either sign. I hold direction at only -20 because the sector has been unwinding on momentum, not thesis, and a stabilisation print could squeeze violently.

what_would_change_my_mind: Evidence of end-market destocking or a peer-chemicals guidance cut in the quarter, which would make the positive reaction history a stale artefact of an easier macro.
reasoning: The only signal here that is not legible is the reaction base rate, and it is genuinely lopsided: one negative in six, mean roughly +3%. That plus a modest consensus bar gets me over the Neutral threshold, but barely, because the +5.6% five-day run-up cuts the other way and the stock sits near its highs rather than in a hole. The Zacks preview I read adds only confirmation of what is already in the price. Sizing: 37.6% realised vol is about 2.4% a day, earnings days run roughly 1.8x, and the 3.9% median agrees, so 4.3%. Medium certainty, because the base-rate signal is stable even if the sample is only six prints.
